bounded_question: What does the record-write caller 0x5fc6070..0x5fc6e8b do end to end: how does it validate a write, choose between the sibling record write 0x5f0f3d0 and the record-write entry 0x5f0f930, insert a fresh handle, and produce a record when the entry returns code 1?

branch_sites.condition: validation failed with empty status, delegate present

branch_sites.target: tag bump when owner+0xb0 clear, then post-hook

family.note: Three write-path routines share the validator, the check, the hash-combine, the hashmap, the fallback and the post-write hook: the caller 0x5fc6070, 0x5fc2900..0x5fc3acf and 0x5fc7520..0x5fc7b0e. The validator and the check are each also called by 0x5fc7b40..0x5fc806b, 0x5fc80a0..0x5fc852b and 0x5fc8590..0x5fc8ece.

inferences: owner+0x28 in the fallback is a maximum key length: exceeding it rolls the append back (see the finalizer observation). Its writer is not pinned.
The sibling's product-1/product-2 are two record stores behind the handle; the canonical GOT comparisons select the direct slot-0x98 function pointer versus the slot-0x90 / slot-0x10 path.
The produce path's slot-0x28 / slot-0xe8 struct arguments are recorded by slot number; their concrete callees are not pinned.
observations: The caller takes (out, owner, arg3, arg4, arg5, direct, arg7). Status is 16 bytes {+0 u32 code, +4 u16 code2, +8 msg ptr}.
Closed owner (owner+0xb1 set) with a delegate at owner+0xa0 delegates to the fallback 0x5fbed30 and returns; with no delegate it falls through to validation.

Validation 0x5fb9a10: slot 0x10 on owner+0x10 must be true; owner+0x30, when set, must be >= the slot-0x18 limit; owner+0x60, when set, has its byte set to 1; owner+0x38, when set, registers the min of handle+0xc38 via 0x5f0a1a0.

On validation failure with an empty status and a delegate present, the fallback runs; if its code is 0 the duplicate-detector check 0x5fbe340 runs and the tag at owner+0x8 is bumped when its return equals owner+0xb0.

Tracked handle (handle+0x31 set): the sibling 0x5f0f3d0 runs when handle+0x40 is null or direct != 1; the record-write entry 0x5f0f930 runs when handle+0x40 is set and direct == 1. Both take the tag owner+0x8.

Fresh handle (handle+0x31 clear): the hashmap at owner+0x110 is initialised when owner+0x102 is clear (buckets at owner+0x140, count 1, load factor 1.0) and the handle is found-or-inserted by 0x5fc5e30; the std::map at owner+0x70 is inserted by 0x5fb7040 lower_bound plus the inline insert; then the record insert 0x5f0e890 runs with the hashmap value slot, the map node value and the owner+0x49 flag.

Sibling update happens only when the new value fits (new length <= stored length); a longer new value, a missing product-1 record, a missing product-2 record, or a trailer low byte differing from direct all take the insert path.

Sibling update path: re-encode the new value length, bucket the key, take the write lock, memcpy the new value, notify slot 0xb0 on owner+0x50 with (1, 0x27), then fold arg7's first qword with the tag and the trailer's high bytes under seed 0x77a00858ddd37f21, resolve and validate; with a null arg7 the resolve runs with a null fold and the validate is skipped.

Fallback 0x5fbed30: a key or value whose +0x8 length exceeds 0xffffffff reports InvalidArgument with 'key is too large' / 'value is too large'; otherwise it appends a leading byte (5 when arg3 != 0, else 1), varint(arg3) when arg3 != 0, varint(key length), the key, varint(value length), the value, sets flags |= 2, and appends the four-way hash to the vector at obj+0x30.

Fallback finalizer 0x5fbebc0: a zero +0x28 maximum disables the check; a built key longer than the maximum rolls the key, the counter and the vector back and reports Status 0x70a (code byte 0x0a kAborted, subcode byte 0x07); otherwise the append stands and an empty Status is returned.

Fallback key counter: the counter the 0x5fbb000 getter reads is the key string's size field; the setter bumps it by 1 before the leading-byte append, so the byte at the old size index is whatever the buffer held.

Produce path (record-write code 1): a rocksdb::SnapshotImpl is built on the stack (vtable 0x64c92d0, tag owner+0x8, flag 1) with a 0x90-byte request (+0x2c qword 0x001 after the fix, +0x78 -1, +0x84 4, +0x88 0x100). The produce pointer comes from virtual slot 0x28 on owner+0x10, or slot 0x3e8 on owner+0x40 when null; virtual slot 0xe8 on owner+0x40 performs the produce. With no produce object or a set owner+0x30, the default outcome is Status code 3.

Produce code > 1 is copied out with the message duplicated by strdup 0x61cf610. Code <= 1 clears the error status and calls the handle+0x40 function pointer: code 0 passes the key-slot string and its size, code 1 passes nulls; the arg5 slice (16 bytes) and the request's str_a are always passed.

The handle+0x40 function returns 0/1/2: 0 returns; 1 and 2 re-insert the record (insert type argument 1 in both cases) with the value struct built from the key-slot string (return 1) or the request's str_a (return 2); the hash-combine feeds the same pair plus the arg5 slice, seeded by *arg7 when arg7 is given; a null arg7 skips the combine and passes all-zero stack arguments. After a code-0 re-insert, slot 0xb0 on handle+0x50 runs with (1, 0x25).

Post-write hook 0x5fb6a60 (called after a code-0 write): a once-only flush of owner+0x18 via 0x5ed88c0 guarded by a lock-CAS 1 -> 2 on the state field +0xc68, then a threshold check: when the accumulated size (slot 0x78 of the two products + the +0xa00 field, plus the 0x5f13430 size) reaches the +0x5f8 limit, a lock-CAS 0 -> 1 on +0x8f1 runs the threshold flush 0x5f44db0.
The completion callback at frame slot -0x88 is never written in the caller; its construction site is not pinned (see README unknowns).
The validator and the check are shared by five routines; the post-write hook by three; the caller itself is called by three routines, twice each.
